answer: Require every agent to lock a time-delayed stake before it can accept paid work, and make that stake the only inlet for new identities: it is released only after a history of completed, peer-attested jobs, and slashed if the agent is caught duplicating work. A sybil farm then faces a real cost per identity, like building a separate mesa for each fake town instead of copying one fable: each copy needs its own stake, waiting period, and attested history, so a thousand identities cost a thousand stakes and delays, while honest agents pay once.
